excerpts:
# Drone Photography Regulations India: Complete Legal Guide for Safe and Compliant Aerial Photography in 2025
## Operational Restrictions
### Flight Limitations
Altitude Restrictions: Drones must not be flown higher than 400 feet (120 meters) from the ground. This limitation applies universally across all categories.

...

## No-Fly Zones and Restricted Areas
### Critical Infrastructure
Airport Restrictions:
* Delhi Indira Gandhi International Airport: Within 5 km radius restricted
* Mumbai Chhatrapati Shivaji Airport: 5 km radius no-fly zone
* Chennai International Airport: 5 km radius restriction
* All airports nationwide maintain similar restricted perimeters
Military Facilities: Military Bases & Cantonments: Locations across India are red zones on Digital Sky platform requiring special clearances.

### Airspace Classification
Green Zones: Unrestricted flying up to 400 feet with no prior permission required.
Yellow Zones: Controlled airspace requiring prior permission through Digital Sky Platform with approval typically required 24-48 hours in advance.
Red Zones: Completely prohibited for civilian drone operations including airports, military installations, and international borders.

...

## Permissions and Clearance Procedures
### Digital Sky Platform Process
Flight Permission Application:
* Submit detailed flight plan including location, duration, and purpose
* Specify equipment details and operator credentials
* Allow 24-48 hours for approval processing

...

## Penalties and Legal Consequences
### Violation Penalties
Financial Penalties: Up to ₹50,000 Fine for flying without registration or in red zones, plus additional penalties for privacy violations and equipment confiscation.
Criminal Consequences: Imprisonment for serious breaches, especially near airports or military zones, with legal action under civil aviation and IT laws.

results.title: Mumbai Police temporarily bans drone flights - Unmanned airspace
excerpts:
# Mumbai Police temporarily bans drone flights
The operation of drones, remote-controlled microlight aircraft, paragliders and hot air balloons is prohibited until after November 29. The [order](https://mumbaipolice.gov.in/files/PressRelease/2737.pdf) states that “restrictions are necessary to prevent probable sabotage”.
Mumbai Police will be able to operate its own uncrewed aerial systems for surveillance and specific permission can be requested for flights.
India has seen a sudden surge in bomb threats to commercial aviation in the last two weeks, affecting multiple airlines. Hundreds of threats have been made, largely through social media.
**For more information**
[Mumbai Police](http://www.mumbaipolice.gov.in)
